permanenceSettings.intro: An operator who keeps the ecosystem running while you do something else. It doesn't decide what to build: it fixes, retries, updates — and it can prove it succeeded, because operations have oracles that the product doesn't. It only runs while the cockpit is open. Everything applies without a button: what you change is saved when you leave the field.

service.title: Service
service.disabledHint: When disabled, the entry leaves the rail: a screen that can't do anything doesn't stay on the menu. Turn it back on here. Pausing, on the other hand, is a gesture — do it from the screen, or with <kbd>⇧P</kbd>.
service.hoursHint: Empty = always. A range that crosses midnight is read as is.
service.cadenceHint: Time between two looks. Empty = 2 minutes.
service.dailyTokensHint: The one it sets for itself. Empty = 200,000.
service.quotaFloorHint: Percentage of subscription quota remaining. Empty = 15%. It works in the background, you in the foreground.
service.catchUp: On wake-up, catch up on what piled up
service.catchUpHint: Unchecked, it starts from scratch and says what it skipped. Catching up on a whole night of signals at once is the surest way to burn through a cap.
service.notifyAllHint: Success is silent, failure speaks: notifying every engagement reopens an inbox, and reading twelve reports is no better than doing the work.

guards.title: Safeguards
guards.intro: Each one answers a specific way things go off the rails, and none replaces the others. They are what makes turning it on bearable.
guards.maxRunningHint: One by default. An on-call operator doesn't handle eight incidents in parallel — and the daily cap doesn't protect against a burst.
guards.rehearsalHint: It decides, writes what it would have done, and doesn't act. The counter resets as soon as you change its powers. Empty = 10.
guards.graceHint: After an engagement, the same PR is left alone. That's what keeps it from waking up on its own commit, and from fixating. Empty = 6 h.
guards.breakerHint: Consecutive failures after which it pauses itself. Re-arming is a gesture: an automatic restart would redo what it exists to prevent. Empty = 3.

role.title: Role
role.intro: Two models, not one. Triage looks at every delta — that's 95% of calls, on tiny inputs; work only starts when an engagement goes out.
role.triageModelHint: The smallest one that can say “nothing”.
role.promptHint: Added to the context of every engagement, on top of the repository dossier.
role.promptPlaceholder: What it should know before acting, whatever the engagement.

rules.title: Rules
rules.intro: Shipped turned off. A rule without a stateable oracle doesn't start, even when on: it's the only stop condition for an agent that has none.
rules.empty: No rules. The Permanence won't do anything until you tell it what to watch.

powers.title: Powers
powers.intro: An allowlist, empty at first, checked one by one. The test: could anyone other than you notice it?
powers.notImplemented: not implemented yet — the gesture will be refused
powers.neverShared: Never on a shared branch. Whatever you check, it never writes to {{branches}}, nor to the base branches declared in your workflow. It only works on its own branches — touching a shared branch isn't an operator's gesture, it's a gesture that commits everyone.
powers.never: Never: {{list}}. These gestures have no tool — they're the ones that commit to a decision, not a report.

comment.title: Comment on a pull request
comment.intro: Never a goal: only the report of an engagement that already has its oracle. It says what it did on the branch, it doesn't start a conversation.
comment.scopesTitle: It only writes where one of these conditions is true
comment.noScope: No condition checked: it won't comment anywhere.
comment.noMonologue: Never two in a row without a human reply in between — otherwise it's a monologue.
comment.signature: Signed <mono>{{signature}}</mono> at the end of the message. Not editable: on a PR, it's your account your colleagues are reading.
comment.optOut: “Stop commenting here” removes a PR in one gesture, without touching the setting.

rule.labelPlaceholder: What it will do, in one line
rule.oracleHint: The proof it aims for, chosen from what this repository declares.
rule.conditionHint: In plain language. Judged at triage, before any engagement.
rule.conditionPlaceholder: the author of the last commit is me
rule.reactionHint: What it attempts. The goal itself is written by it.
rule.reactionPlaceholder: fix it, open a draft PR
rule.delayScheduleHint: Between two runs of this rule. Empty = 24 h.
rule.delayStaleHint: Beyond this, a change is considered stale. Empty = 72 h.
rule.tokenBudgetHint: Per engagement of this rule. Empty = the daily cap.
rule.perHourHint: Empty = only the daily cap applies.
rule.needsApproval: Ask for my approval before the work starts
rule.needsApprovalHint: Without it, it approves the mission plan itself — this rule is the approval. Check it for a high-stakes rule.

test.title: The test we derive from it

What can be checked mechanically doesn't belong here — these are the rules no tool states, the ones passed on by word of mouth.
propertiesSettings.emptyHint: The cockpit can suggest some based on what this repository has already had to fix — that's what it will break again.
propertiesSettings.proposeHint: Read the repository's fixes and derive properties from them
propertiesSettings.textPlaceholder: E.g.: every route that writes to the database validates its body before calling it.

workflow.intro: The columns of your task tracker, named the way your team names them. They decide how far along a ticket is and where it sits in the daily.

blocked.label: Blocked
blocked.hint: the column that signals a blocker

baseBranches.label: Base branches
baseBranches.hint: a PR targeting anything else counts as stacked

prCommand.label: PR opening command
prCommand.hint: run by the lead at the end of a mission; empty = Cockpit opens the PR itself

createWorktree.label: Create a worktree
createWorktree.hint: empty = `git worktree add`. A command starting with "/" is a repository command, run by an agent.

removeWorktree.label: Remove a worktree
removeWorktree.hint: empty = `git worktree remove --force`. Make sure it can't hang on a confirmation prompt: nobody will read it.

workflow.malformed: {{commands}}: a placeholder goes between curly braces. Written any other way, it reaches the shell as is — which rejects the line without a word.

testCommands.label: Test commands
testCommands.hint: on top of vitest, jest, pytest, phpunit, php artisan test… — what lets an agent's card say "tests pass"

visualReports.title: Agents report back with images
visualReports.detail: Checked: every agent is told to show its work when an image says more than text — a before/after screenshot if it changed the screen and can capture it, a diagram if it changed a structure, nothing for a simple answer. Applies to agents launched from now on, not those already running.

agentBrowser.title: Agents drive their workspace's browser
agentBrowser.detail: Checked: every agent gets what it needs to open a page, click, type and take screenshots, in a separate browser — without your sessions or passwords — that you watch live in the "Browser" tab. It only starts on the first action. No effect inside an isolation container. Applies to agents launched from now on.

browser.label: Browser
browser.hint: empty = the first one found among Chrome, Chromium, Edge and Brave

reviewReadOnly.title: The review agent is read-only
reviewReadOnly.detail: Checked: no editing, and nothing but reads (git diff, git log, gh pr view…) — everything else is refused. Unchecked: it can run tests or modify files; its instructions still tell it not to fix the PR, but nothing stops it.

workflow.themes_one: {{count}} business topic declared — it lets the daily say "she's on billing" rather than list identifiers. Topics are edited in the configuration file.
workflow.themes_other: {{count}} business topics declared — they let the daily say "she's on billing" rather than list identifiers. Topics are edited in the configuration file.
workflow.noThemes: No business topics: the daily narrative will rely on the titles themselves.

roles.intro: What a worker receives at launch: its standing instructions, its model, and the paths it is allowed to write to. The scope is enforced — a write outside it is refused, not merely discouraged.
roles.masterNote: This role leads the mission: it reads the ticket, proposes the breakdown and puts everything back together at the end. Its key is reserved — the steps and orchestration tools come from Cockpit; only its command, instructions and model are set here.

depth.label: Depth
depth.hint: how much the role is allowed to spend
depth.unsupported: This engine declares no depth — set them under Engines.

command.label: Startup command
command.hint: repository skill or command, run before the instructions

roles.verifies: Checks the others' work — only starts once the implementation is delivered

team.intro: Who's on the team, and which accounts identify them in each tool. These mappings drive the daily and the team board: a member without their GitHub login won't show up on any pull request.
team.soloWarning: This project is marked solo: its team is ignored and the daily stays hidden. Untick "solo" in the project settings for what follows to be of any use.

linearTeam.label: Linear team
linearTeam.hint: UUID of the team whose current cycle is read — empty = no daily

team.empty: No members declared: the daily and the team board will stay empty. Cockpit suggests no one by default — a team can't be guessed.
team.name: Name

linearId.label: Linear ID
linearId.hint: UUID, visible in their profile URL

engines.intro: An engine is the program that runs an agent — not a model provider. To use another one, there are two ways: a binary that speaks the same protocol, or a compatible gateway designated by the environment variables below. Each role then picks its engine.

binary.label: Binary
binary.hint: empty = claude, looked up on the machine

engines.depthFastHint: what to add to go fast
engines.depthDeepHint: for what deserves the extra effort

env.label: Environment
env.hint: one pair per line: NAME=value — a service address, an access token

engines.variables_one: {{count}} variable — written to the configuration file, with 600 permissions.
engines.variables_other: {{count}} variables — written to the configuration file, with 600 permissions.
engines.noVariables: No variables: the engine uses the machine's environment.

guided.title: Guided
guided.detail: You read the ticket with the lead, then approve its understanding, its approach and its breakdown — three agreements, one at a time.

autonomous.title: Autonomous
autonomous.detail: The lead reads the ticket and proposes its breakdown right away. A single agreement before the workers set off.

budget.intro: Three caps, for three ways of spending more than intended: a mission that runs away, a quota that runs out, a machine that saturates. None of them kills anything — work in progress always runs to completion.

tokenBudget.label: Cap per mission
tokenBudget.hint: Beyond it, the mission pauses — branches and work intact, resumed in one click. Empty = 500,000.

quotaFloor.label: No new starts below
quotaFloor.hint: Percentage of subscription quota remaining. Tasks in progress carry on. Empty = 15%.

memoryCeiling.label: No new launches above
memoryCeiling.hint: Percentage of machine memory in use. No new agent starts — mission, worker or manual launch. Empty = 85%.

sandbox.intro: Each agent runs in a container, with its own memory capped by the system rather than measured after the fact. Requires Docker or OrbStack on the machine — neither is needed while this is off.
sandbox.enable: Isolate each agent in a container

runtime.hint: orb or docker. Empty = detected on the machine.

sandbox.loginNote: An account signed in through a subscription stores its token in the machine's keychain, which a container can't read. This button runs claude setup-token in a terminal — then paste the token it shows into Settings → Access tokens ("Isolated account"). Valid for one year; redo it once it expires.
